mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as market participants anticipate future rate hikes, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the month preceding the decision date
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05), or the inflation spike is not confirmed by subsequent FEDFUNDS hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures that outpace productivity, prompting equity market anticipation of higher earnings and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-on-month increase > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where INDPRO growth exceeds PAYEMS by >0.2% monthly, SPX 60-day forward returns are not positive (mean < 0, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index below 100 (indicating supply-side weakness) coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 for the first time in the current quarter
failure_condition: Over a 20-day window following the trigger, the SPX 20-day forward return is positive in >70% of similar INDPRO contractions (robustness test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% in a month with falling UNRATE unemployment suggests resilient consumer demand, generating a positive 5-day SPX forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-on-month increase > 2% AND UNRATE month-on-month decrease > 0.1%
regime_hint: resilient demand in labor market cooling
failure_condition: Across 100 matched trigger events, the 5-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 4% for three consecutive months creates a risk-off environment, producing negative 20-day SPX forward returns unless offset by strong GDP momentum.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where RSAFS > 700B for 10 consecutive months, the 20-day forward return is not negative (mean > 0, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4.0% accompanied by a 3-month decline in PAYEMS labor costs suggests softening labor market strength, resulting in a negative 60-day SPX forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% AND PAYEMS month-on-month decline for three months
failure_condition: Across 50 matched trigger events, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in RSAFS industrial production index below 700M for two consecutive months, without a parallel rise in GDPC1 demand, predicts a negative 20-day SPX forward return as supply chain bottlenecks persist.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 700M for two consecutive months AND GDPC1 does not increase by >5% in the same months
failure_condition: In 100 matched supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is positive in >40% of cases (robustness).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle is signaled by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and CPIAUCSL accelerating above 2% for two consecutive months, producing a positive 60-day SPX forward return as markets price in higher future rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL month-on-month increase > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 matched tightening signals, the 60-day forward return mean is not positive (p > 0.05), or the regime is not confirmed by a subsequent 3-month FEDFUNDS hold at >4.5%.
